While this approach can accelerate prototyping, brainstorming, and learning, it may fall short when it comes to producing robust, maintainable, and secure production-level software—unless it's backed by rigorous testing, code review, and documentation.

For professional development, vibe coding can be a valuable tool in the early stages of development or when exploring new solutions. However, relying solely on vibe coding without deeper understanding or structured practices would not meet the professional standards expected in most software engineering environments.
